dimensions.analysis: The candidate never read the failing test body or discussed what behavior was expected for partially-shipped holds. They went straight from a failing test run to guessing at a file location without resolving any ambiguity about what the correct release quantity should be.

The stated plan was only a vague location guess ("something in the sweep file"), not a mechanism. They never articulated the hypothesis that the sweep releases the original count instead of the remaining count before editing.

Aside from the initial vague guess and a closing remark that it passes, there is no narration of what was read in sweep.ts, what was suspected, or what the edit actually changed. The transcript alone does not explain the path taken.

A single edit was made to src/sweep.ts and saved, and the test suite subsequently passed, suggesting the edit did land on the correct fix area. However, with no stated plan and no narration of the change, it's impossible to assess whether the implementation was a scoped, deliberate fix or a lucky guess.

They did re-run the test suite after the edit and observed a passing result before ending the session, meeting the minimal bar of checking work before declaring success. There is no evidence of checking edge cases or confirming that full-release behavior remained correct.

The closing remark was a bare acknowledgment that tests passed, with no explanation of the root cause (phantom stock from releasing original count instead of remaining count) or why the fix addressed it. This falls short of articulating the failure mechanism.
